source_text: 1. Ἐπεὶ (δὲ) περὶ τηλικούτων ἐξετάζοντες πραγμάτων, οὐχ ἀρχούμενοι ταῖς κοιναῖς ἐνγοίαις καὶ τῇ ἐναργείᾳ τῶν βλεπομένων, προσπαραλαμβάνομεν εἰς τὴν φαινομένην ἡμῖν ἀπόδειξιν τῶν λεγομένων μαρτύρια τὰ ἐκ τῶν πεπιστευμένων ἡμῖν εἶναι ϑείων γραφῶν, τῆς τε λεγομένης παλαιᾶς διαϑήκης καὶ τῆς καλουμένης καινῆς, λόγῳ τε πειρώμεθα χρατύνειν ἡμῶν τὴν πίστιν, καὶ οὐδέπω περὶ τῶν γραφῶν ὡς ϑείων διελέχϑημεν᾽ φέρε καὶ περὶ τούτων ὀλίγα ὡς ἐν ἐπιτομῇ διαλάβωμεν, τὰ κινοῦντα ἡμᾶς Oc περὶ ϑείων γραμμάτων εἰς τοῦτο παρατιϑέμενοι. καὶ πρῶτόν γε, (πρὸ) τοῦ ar αὐτῶν τῶν γραμμάτων xoi τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς δηλουμένων ῥητοῖς χρήσασϑαι, περὶ Μωσέως καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ νομοϑέτου τῶν Ἑβραίων καὶ τοῦ εἰσηγητοῦ τῶν χατὰ χριστιανισμὸν σωτηρίων δογμάτων, ταῦτα διαληπτέον.
pass_a_gloss: Since we are investigating such things, not being led by the common accusations and the clearness of the things seen, we take up as evidence for the apparent proof of the things being said the testimonies from the writings believed by us to be divine, both the so-called old covenant and the so-called new, and we try to strengthen our faith with a word, and we have not yet discussed the writings as divine; come and let us take up a few things about these in brief, the things moving us concerning divine writings, placing them before this. And first, before using the writings themselves and the expressions in them, the things about Moses and Jesus Christ, the lawgiver of the Hebrews and the introducer of the saving doctrines according to Christianity, must be taken up.
pass_b_english: Since we are investigating matters of this magnitude, we do not rely on common accusations or the obvious evidence of what is seen; instead, we bring forward as evidence for the apparent proof of what is being said the testimonies from the writings we believe to be divine — both the so-called Old Covenant and the so-called New — and we attempt to strengthen our faith by means of a word. We have not yet discussed the writings as divine; come, then, and let us take up a few things about them in brief, setting before ourselves the considerations that move us concerning divine writings. First, before we use the writings themselves and the expressions within them, we must address the matter of Moses and Jesus Christ, the lawgiver of the Hebrews and the introducer of the saving doctrines according to Christianity.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex syntax of the Greek. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the negation 'οὐχ ἀρχούμενοι' (not being led / do not rely) and the conditional/causal structure. Pass B provides a more fluent rendering of 'τὰ κινοῦντα ἡμᾶς' as 'the considerations that move us', which is a valid interpretation of the participle. All theological and historical designations (lawgiver of the Hebrews, etc.) are preserved.
